Description: Create HF account; accept terms on bharatgenai/Shrutam-2, bharatgenai/sooktam2, ai4bharat/indictrans2-indic-en-1B and en-indic-1B. Generate access token; set HF_TOKEN env var. Async, before Day 1.
Rationale (why this is here): All three target models are gated or trust_remote_code. Token must be live before Day 1 or first model load fails.

Description: Create RunPod account. Spin up a Pod with persistent volume attached (recommend 80-100 GB to fit HF cache for all 3 models + datasets). GPU template: RTX 4090 (24 GB, cheaper) or A40 (48 GB, headroom for Week 6 multi-model). Note: pod ID, volume ID, GPU type chosen — documented in repo README.
Rationale (why this is here): Inference benchmarks are meaningful only against a fixed environment. Pod + GPU template should not change across weeks. Persistent volume so models survive pod restarts (otherwise re-downloading IndicTrans2-1B + Shrutam-2 + Sooktam-2 every cold start wastes 30+ min).
Notes: Account created, pod will be created when required since it consumes credits

Description: On the Pod: `export HF_HOME=/workspace/.cache/huggingface` (or whatever the mount path is). Add to ~/.bashrc. Verify by loading a tiny model and checking the file lands on the persistent volume.
Rationale (why this is here): Default HF cache lives in container ephemeral storage — wiped on pod restart. Pointing HF_HOME at the volume means model downloads are one-time. This single line saves ~5 hours over the internship.

Description: Create `bharatgen-speech-intern-2026` with week0/ through week7/ folders. Branch protection so reviews are mandatory.
Rationale (why this is here): Weekly commits make progress visible asynchronously. Removes the 'I lost my notebook' failure mode.

Description: Python 3.10, conda or uv, VS Code with Python + Jupyter extensions, ffmpeg, jupyter lab.
Rationale (why this is here): ffmpeg is a hidden dependency for librosa/torchaudio/soundfile. Installing on Day 0 avoids a Day-1 audio-loading bug that looks unrelated.

Description: AI4Bharat blog post on IndicTTS/IndicASR. Skim Shrutam-2 + Sooktam-2 model cards. No notes required.
Rationale (why this is here): Builds vocabulary exposure so Day 3 concepts have anchor points. Retention is not the goal here.
Notes: Mark Done at end of Week 0 — vocabulary surfaces correctly in reflection.md (attention, transformers)

Item: Day 1: numpy - arrays, shape, dtype, broadcasting
Description: How arrays differ from Python lists. What .shape and .dtype mean. Broadcasting rules: when do (3,1) and (1,4) combine to (3,4).
Rationale (why this is here): PyTorch tensors are numpy arrays + GPU + autograd. Master numpy first; PyTorch then feels 30% new, not 100% new.

Description: Cell execution order, kernel state, %time, %matplotlib inline. Why notebooks for exploration, scripts for production.
Rationale (why this is here): ML work lives in notebooks. Notebook mental model is different from script mental model — hidden kernel state causes 'works for me' bugs.

Description: Create arrays, slice, broadcast, dot product, reshape. 10 small exercises. Write down what .shape will be BEFORE running each cell.
Rationale (why this is here): Predicting shape before running is the discipline that prevents 80% of 'shape mismatch' bugs later.

Description: Create a fresh venv with uv or conda, install numpy/matplotlib/jupyter, freeze a requirements.txt.
Rationale (why this is here): Every later week installs more packages. Environment hygiene now prevents 'it worked yesterday' problems in Week 4.

Description: fig, ax = plt.subplots(). plot(), scatter(), hist(), set_xlabel/set_ylabel/set_title.
Rationale (why this is here): Every week involves plotting something. Familiarity removes a recurring friction point.

Description: Plot a sine wave, a 1000-sample Gaussian histogram, a scatter of two correlated variables. Each plot labeled.
Rationale (why this is here): Three plot types cover ~80% of what he'll plot. Practiced once, available always.

Item: Day 2: read one library doc page end-to-end
Description: librosa 'Core IO and DSP' page. Read every section. Try one example from each.
Rationale (why this is here): Reading docs is THE skill. Practicing it on a library he'll use next week is dual-purpose.

Item: Day 3: what is a 'model' in ML
Description: A function with learned parameters. Input -> some math -> output. That's it for now. We won't train any — only run pre-trained ones.
Rationale (why this is here): Demystifies the word. Removes the 'how does it learn' anxiety which is not Week 0's problem.

Item: Day 3: what is a tensor (vs numpy array)
Description: Same data structure (n-dim array of numbers), but: lives on GPU, tracks gradients (we won't use this in inference). For our purposes: numpy array on a graphics card.
Rationale (why this is here): 90% of 'PyTorch feels hard' is this conceptual confusion. Naming and dismissing it early saves a week.

Description: Converts text -> list of integers (tokens) so models can process it. Different models have different tokenizers. 'नमस्ते' might be 1 token or 5 tokens depending on the tokenizer.
Rationale (why this is here): Crucial framing for Weeks 2-5 where tokenizers appear repeatedly. One-paragraph mental model is enough.

Description: Training: model learns from labeled data. Inference: model runs on new inputs. We do inference only for 7 weeks. Knowing what we're NOT doing scopes the work.
Rationale (why this is here): Bounds the scope explicitly. Pre-empts the 'should I train it' instinct that derails most first ML projects.

Description: GPU = thousands of small parallel cores, great at matrix multiplications. CPU = few fast sequential cores. Neural network = millions of matmuls -> GPU is 10-100x faster.
Rationale (why this is here): Frames Day 5's GPU warm-up and every subsequent profiling discussion. Intuition first, mechanics later.

Description: But what IS a Neural Network?', 'Gradient descent', 'What does backpropagation really do?'. ~60 min total. Watch, don't pause to implement.
Rationale (why this is here): Visual intuition for what's inside the model box. Watching is enough; implementing is for later if at all.

Description: Answer in his own words: 'What is a neural network? What does training mean? Why do we need data?' One page max.
Rationale (why this is here): Watching != understanding. Writing in own words tests retention and exposes gaps cheaply. THIS is the bootstrap diagnostic.

Description: Single page only: transformers are a NN architecture good at sequences. Attention lets each token 'look at' other tokens. Read Jay Alammar 'Illustrated Transformer' intro (first 1/3 only).
Rationale (why this is here): One-page bird's-eye view so transformer vocabulary in Weeks 2-5 isn't entirely foreign. Don't go deep.

Description: pip install torch. torch.tensor([1,2,3]). Move .to('cuda'). Print .shape, .dtype, .device. Matmul of two random 1000x1000 tensors on CPU vs GPU, time both.
Rationale (why this is here): Tactile first PyTorch experience. CPU-vs-GPU timing makes the Day-3 'why GPU' concept concrete.
Notes: torch.tensor created, moved to/from cuda; .shape/.dtype/.device printed

Item: Day 5: run HF distilbert via pipeline()
Description: from transformers import pipeline; pipe = pipeline('sentiment-analysis'); pipe('I love this'). Three lines. Print the output.
Rationale (why this is here): Easiest possible HF entry. No AutoModel/AutoTokenizer yet — just see that 'model goes brrr' works.
Notes: pipeline('sentiment-analysis') run on 2 sentences with prose explanation of the load/tokenize/inference flow

Description: Commit week0_bootstrap.ipynb to repo with all Day 1-5 exercises. First git push.
Rationale (why this is here): Repo hygiene begins. Friday review now has something to review.
Notes: Multiple commits to claude/setup-intern-project-FkRbX; week0_bootstrap.ipynb + day notebooks pushed

Description: Single notebook covering Days 1-5 exercises. reflection.md = his 1-page NN explanation from Day 4.
Rationale (why this is here): Single artifact for the week. Reviewable in one sitting. Reflection.md is the diagnostic — if vague, slow Week 1 down.
Notes: Consolidated 60-cell bootstrap notebook + reflection.md (NN, training, why-data, GD, backprop, attention/transformers) committed

Item: Don't: implement a NN from scratch
Description: Skip 'build your own neural network in numpy' tutorials. Skip backprop derivations.
Rationale (why this is here): Optimization target for Week 0 is conceptual coverage, not building. Implementation is a Week-9+ activity (i.e., after this internship).
Notes: No scratch-NN implementation in week0 notebooks

Description: Skip 'Autograd', 'Training a Classifier', 'Optimization'. Those are training-stack content; we don't train.
Rationale (why this is here): Inference-only scope. Reading training content now muddles the mental model.
Notes: Day 5 stayed at tensor creation + device moves; no autograd

Description: If gradient descent algebra is hard, that's fine. Watch for intuition; math doesn't gate Week 1.
Rationale (why this is here): Math fluency is not a Week-0 prerequisite. Sets expectations.

Description: What sampling rate means; why ASR models specify 16 kHz; what happens when you pass 44.1 kHz to a 16 kHz model.
Rationale (why this is here): Sample-rate mismatch is a top silent-failure mode. Spot it now, save 4 hours of debugging later.

Description: Why speech models expect mono. How to convert stereo to mono in librosa/torchaudio.
Rationale (why this is here): Common preprocessing bug source.

Description: Visual difference; what models actually consume; why mel rather than linear frequency.
Rationale (why this is here): Models consume spectrograms, humans see waveforms. Bridging this gap visually = fastest path to intuition.

Description: tensor.to(device), .shape, .dtype, .cpu(), .numpy(). Why device-mismatched ops fail.
Rationale (why this is here): Builds on Week 0 Day 5 with more depth now that bootstrap context exists.

Description: Phone recordings: Hindi, English, plus 3 of Marathi/Tamil/Kannada/Bengali. Save as WAV.
Rationale (why this is here): Real audio surfaces real preprocessing issues that synthetic test files don't.

Description: Side-by-side plots in librosa. Zoom in on silence vs speech. Annotate which is which.
Rationale (why this is here): Visualization grounds the abstract. Annotation forces him to articulate what he sees.

Description: torchaudio.transforms.Resample. Listen and compare. Note what's lost.
Rationale (why this is here): Demonstrates that significant information loss is tolerable for intelligibility — frames why ASR standardized on 16 kHz.

Description: 10000x10000 matmul, CPU vs GPU. Compare to Week 0 Day 5's 1000x1000 numbers.
Rationale (why this is here): Quantifies how the gap grows with size. Concrete intuition for batching benefits later.

Description: Notebook with plots and annotations. 1-page cheatsheet: sampling rate, mono/stereo, resampling, mel-spectrogram.
Rationale (why this is here): Cheatsheet seeds the handoff package. Audience-of-two forces clarity.

Description: Skip the full course. Theory rabbit hole.
Rationale (why this is here): Three weeks can disappear into lectures with no code shipped.

Description: Pattern-match what librosa produces. Don't reinvent the FFT.
Rationale (why this is here): Not on the critical path to running BharatGen models.

Description: The Auto* pattern in HF transformers. Three classes: model weights, text tokenizer, multimodal processor.
Rationale (why this is here): Once internalized, every new HF model card becomes 80% familiar.

Description: What this flag does: executes Python from the model repo. Implications for untrusted models.
Rationale (why this is here): Sooktam-2 in Week 4 requires this flag. Need intuition before flipping it.

Description: Training mode vs inference mode. no_grad halves memory and speeds up inference because it stops tracking gradients.
Rationale (why this is here): Forgotten in ~50% of beginner inference code. Easy win.

Item: Tokens, logits, softmax - the output side
Description: Token = integer the tokenizer produces. Logits = raw model output (one number per vocab token). Softmax converts logits to probabilities. Builds on Week 0 tokenizer concept.
Rationale (why this is here): Closes the loop on Week 0. Logits/softmax are the language of every generate() call.

Description: Inspect ~/.cache/huggingface/hub/. Files: config.json, tokenizer files, weights.
Rationale (why this is here): Demystifies the 'magic' of from_pretrained. Helps diagnose disk-space issues later.

Description: Load distilbert with AutoModel/AutoTokenizer. Print raw logits, apply torch.softmax, see probabilities. Compare to pipeline()'s output.
Rationale (why this is here): Bridges Week 0's pipeline() experience with the manual API. He sees what pipeline() was doing.

Description: openai/whisper-tiny via transformers. Get transcriptions.
Rationale (why this is here): First speech model. Becomes Week 3 baseline for Shrutam-2 comparison.

Description: Identify and write in plain English what hidden_size, num_hidden_layers, vocab_size mean.
Rationale (why this is here): Builds intuition for what 'loading a model' actually involves.

Description: Tutorial written FOR the next intern. Code, screenshots, pipeline() vs manual loading.
Rationale (why this is here): Writing-for-others is the strongest test of understanding.

Description: No LoRA, no PEFT, no full fine-tune. Inference-only.
Rationale (why this is here): Half-trained models with no documentation. Inference depth > training breadth here.

Description: Skip distributed and quantization libraries.
Rationale (why this is here): Premature optimization. Adds debugging surface without value.

Description: (insertions + deletions + substitutions) / reference length. Use jiwer library.
Rationale (why this is here): Only quantitative way to compare ASR systems.

Description: Why Hindi-English code-mix breaks most ASR models: tokenizer coverage, training-data distribution.
Rationale (why this is here): India-specific. Where BharatGen most differentiates from Whisper.

Description: Greedy = take highest-probability token each step. Beam = keep top-k partial sequences. One paragraph each.
Rationale (why this is here): Affects every .generate() call. Enough to know what knob to tweak.

Description: 10 Hindi + 10 Tamil + 5 code-mixed clips. Real audio (YouTube, podcasts, his own recordings), NOT model card examples.
Rationale (why this is here): Real audio surfaces real failure modes. Model card examples are cherry-picked.

Description: Same audio, same ground truth, both models. Tabulate WER per language.
Rationale (why this is here): Shrutam-2 in isolation is just numbers. Comparison gives meaning.

Description: torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated(), wall-clock time, audio-seconds per inference-second. Note hardware and batch size.
Rationale (why this is here): Inference-stack thinking starts here. Discipline reused every subsequent week.

Description: WER table, profiling table, 5 transcription failures with his hypothesis on each.
Rationale (why this is here): 'Why did it fail?' forces reasoning about model behavior.

Description: No retraining, no domain adaptation. Evaluation only.
Rationale (why this is here): Improvement is meaningless before measurement is solid.

Item: Don't: report numbers without hardware context
Description: Always note GPU, batch size, audio length, language.
Rationale (why this is here): A latency number without context is noise.

Description: A vector of numbers representing something (a token, a speaker, an image). Similar things -> similar vectors. Speaker embedding = vector representing one person's voice.
Rationale (why this is here): Foundational concept used everywhere from here. Defining explicitly prevents confusion in Week 4 onwards.

Description: Sooktam-2 takes a reference WAV + reference transcript and produces a speaker embedding. The TTS is conditioned on it — output mimics the reference voice.
Rationale (why this is here): Distinguishes Sooktam-2 from description-conditioned TTS like Indic Parler.

Description: Acoustic model: text -> mel-spectrogram. Vocoder: mel-spectrogram -> waveform. Two stages, two failure modes.
Rationale (why this is here): Helps reason about quality failures. Buzzy = vocoder. Wrong pronunciation = acoustic model. Different fixes.

Description: RTF = generation_time / audio_duration. RTF < 1 = faster than real-time.
Rationale (why this is here): Standard TTS metric. Lets him compare Sooktam-2 to Indic Parler on a common axis.

Description: Hindi + Marathi + Tamil; three different reference speakers per language.
Rationale (why this is here): Reveals model behavior across language and speaker dimensions.

Description: Long target text (>500 chars). English loanwords in Hindi. Numbers and currency (2026, Rs.450). Code-mixed input.
Rationale (why this is here): These are where production deployments break. Document now.

Description: Same Hindi sentences, same listener. Reference-conditioned vs description-conditioned paradigms.
Rationale (why this is here): Forces articulating the trade-off.

Description: Same profiling discipline as Week 3.
Rationale (why this is here): Builds the habit.

Description: Markdown + committed audio. Indic Parler comparison. Tabulated profiling. Edge-case failure samples.
Rationale (why this is here): Claims about audio quality MUST be backed by listenable artifacts.

Description: Every quality assertion links to a WAV file.
Rationale (why this is here): Untestable claims become folk wisdom.

Item: Don't: forget reference clip quality is a ceiling
Description: A noisy/unclear reference produces mediocre output regardless of model.
Rationale (why this is here): Garbage in, garbage out. Common beginner error.

Description: Input sequence -> output sequence. ASR is audio-seq -> text-seq. TTS is text-seq -> audio-seq. Translation is text-seq -> text-seq. Same family.
Rationale (why this is here): Naming the abstraction unifies three apparently different models. Reduces cognitive load.

Description: Encoder = reads the whole input and builds an internal representation. Decoder = generates output one token at a time, looking at encoder's representation.
Rationale (why this is here): Architecture intuition for why translation models look different from chatbot LLMs.

Description: Generates token by token, each new token depends on previously generated tokens. Builds on Week 2 logits/softmax: at each step, model outputs logits, picks next token.
Rationale (why this is here): Connects to earlier softmax concept. Explains why latency scales with output length.

Description: Now actually set num_beams=1, 4, 8. Observe output and latency changes.
Rationale (why this is here): Week 3 introduced concept; Week 5 experiences it.

Description: ai4bharat/indictrans2-indic-en-1B and en-indic-1B. 30 sentences across 4 languages.
Rationale (why this is here): Practical breadth.

Description: Technical/legal Hindi, casual WhatsApp text, numbers and dates, code-mixed input.
Rationale (why this is here): Tests robustness across registers.

Description: Hindi -> English -> Hindi for 10 sentences. Compare to originals for meaning drift.
Rationale (why this is here): Quick quality signal without expensive BLEU.

Description: Same profiling discipline.
Rationale (why this is here): Continuity.

Description: Eval doc + a small CLI: `python translate.py --src hi --tgt en --text "..."`.
Rationale (why this is here): First reusable tool. Imported into Week 6 pipeline.

Item: Don't: treat BLEU as the only metric
Description: BLEU + round-trip + human spot-checks.
Rationale (why this is here): BLEU is brittle for morphologically rich Indic languages.

Description: How models compose. State between models (audio buffers, intermediate text, language metadata).
Rationale (why this is here): Composition has its own failure modes that individual models don't.

Description: Three models, finite GPU. Decision: keep all loaded, swap, or offload to CPU? Trade-offs.
Rationale (why this is here): The inference-stack lesson. The engineering judgment is what we want him to develop.

Description: Audio -> Shrutam-2 (Hindi audio -> Hindi text) -> IndicTrans2 (Hindi -> English) -> Sooktam-2 (English text -> English audio).
Rationale (why this is here): The actual goal of the internship.

Description: File or mic input, source/target language dropdowns, audio player output. Run on localhost.
Rationale (why this is here): Makes the demo accessible to non-engineers.

Description: All three loaded? Lazy load? Evict between calls? Pick one, defend in writing, document.
Rationale (why this is here): Defending the choice is more valuable than picking the optimal one.

Description: Empty transcription. Very long input audio (>5 min). Translation timeout.
Rationale (why this is here): Bounded scope. Three well > fifteen poorly.

Description: End-to-end wall clock for a 10s audio input. Per-stage breakdown.
Rationale (why this is here): Sets up Week 7's end-to-end profiling.

Description: Hand-drawn architecture: data flow, model placements, memory budget, failure modes.
Rationale (why this is here): Drawing tests data-flow understanding.

Description: No WebSockets. Request-response only.
Rationale (why this is here): Streaming is its own multi-week project.

Description: No Docker. Plain Python + Gradio.
Rationale (why this is here): Containerization without deployment target is theater.

Description: For a 10s Hindi -> English audio task: total ms, ASR ms, translate ms, TTS ms, overhead ms. Single diagram.
Rationale (why this is here): Synthesizes every week's profiling. The diagram goes on the wall.

Description: Peak GPU memory per model. Peak with all three loaded concurrently. Implication: GPU tier needed.
Rationale (why this is here): Concrete answer to a recurring product question.

Description: Language coverage, code-mix failures, accent sensitivity, translation degradation, latency bottlenecks, GPU memory ceiling.
Rationale (why this is here): Honest scoping. Next intern starts knowing what doesn't work.

Description: Root README.md: 'How to run this in 30 minutes from scratch.' Step-by-step.
Rationale (why this is here): If new intern can't get to a working demo in 30 min, handoff failed.

Description: SETUP: env/GPU/HF tokens. EXPERIMENTS: tried, worked, didn't. NEXT_STEPS: three concrete projects for next intern.
Rationale (why this is here): Decomposes the handoff into discoverable pieces.

Description: Screen recording: demo the pipeline, walk through repo, point at limitations.
Rationale (why this is here): Watching is faster than reading for first-touch onboarding.

Description: git tag v1.0-intern-handoff. Final mentor review.
Rationale (why this is here): Discrete milestone. 'Done' is unambiguous.

Item: Don't: leave docs for the last day
Description: Docs accumulate weekly from Week 1.
Rationale (why this is here): Week-7-only doc writing misses ~30% of what was done.
